Redwood to provide Privatelink vs peering cost estimate and region availability
action_items: Maya: send sample benchmark harness and synthetic load scripts (due 2028-07-18)
Jon: export VPC CIDR blocks and security group owner contacts (due 2028-07-17)

header:
Date: 2028-07-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Samira Voss (Redwood CSM), Amira Patel (Pinetree Head of Platform), Jon Ruiz (SRE), Grace Liu (Security), Owen Park (CTO)
summary: POC scoping for an "islanded" private-network deployment. Main topics: peering vs PrivateLink topology, region lock and egress constraints, success metrics (latency/p99, throughput qps), workload sizing for genomics-ish inference bursts, benchmark plan and timeline. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot with synthetic and replayed traffic; Redwood to share runbook and scripts, customer to share network diagram and compliance artifacts.
topics: Topology: VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs endpoint isolation
Workload sizing: peak bursts, sustained qps, model context lengths
Benchmarks: synthetic vs replay, p50/p95/p99 targets, percentiles and token throughput
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, i know it's afternoon for some of you, appreciate you carving out the time. quick round of intros?
[00:12] Amira Patel: yeah hi i'm amira, i run platform at Pinetree, and i'll own the pilot internal coordination. sorry for the background noise.
[00:20] Owen Park: owen, cto, i'll be high-level, but jon and grace will drive the details.
[00:28] Jon Ruiz: jon, s r e. we'll be hands-on for networking and benching.
[00:34] Grace Liu: grace, security. we'll need SOC2, audit logs, and K M S integration details.
[00:42] Luis Ortega: great, i'm luis, i'll cover topology and the bench approach from redwood.
[00:48] Maya Chen: goal for today: agree success criteria, pick topology for pilot (peering vs privatelink vs endpoint isolation), and agree bench plan + timeline.
[01:02] Amira Patel: our main constraint is we must keep data in-region and not egress to public internet. also traffic must not traverse any third-party networks, so peering preferred but we have strict firewall rules.
[01:15] Luis Ortega: understood. quick clarifier: by peering you mean direct VPC peering to redwood's inference VPC in the same cloud account, or peering to Redwood's managed VPC in our partner region? there's a few variants.
[01:30] Amira Patel: ideally direct peering into your managed VPC in our account, but if that's not possible, privatelink endpoints in our account are acceptable. we prefer not to expose NAT egress.
[01:43] Maya Chen: note: Redwood Private supports both — we call it Redwood Private (VPC-mode) — and we can do privatelink endpoints. there's tradeoffs: peering tends to give lower latency and easier throughput, privatelink gives better isolation and customer's control over endpoints.
[01:57] Owen Park: cost question: is privatelink significantly more expensive?
[02:02] Luis Ortega: yes there's per-endpoint cost plus data processing fees, peering is typically cheaper for sustained bandwidth. but if you need strict isolation and route controls, privatelink simplifies the egress fence.
[02:18] Grace Liu: from compliance: we need audit logs for every call, key management (bring your own KMS or H S M), and proof tokens are not persisted outside region. is that supported?
[02:31] Maya Chen: yes we support BYOK via KMS, and we can enable audit logs to your log collector via a secure delivery path. small note: some customers call it redwood privet in docs, transcript might show that wrong.
[02:45] Jon Ruiz: ok on the bench: our workload is bursty — peaks of ~1200 concurrent requests for 90s, then idle periods. models: mostly 8k context generative but a few heavy 16k rerank flows. we need p99 under 300ms for the 8k is ideal.
[03:05] Luis Ortega: ping — 1200 concurrent, is that QPS or sockets?
[03:10] Jon Ruiz: that's concurrent open sessions, roughly 600 qps during the peak depending on token lengths.
[03:16] Luis Ortega: good. for piloting we'll size GPU pools to mimic that: we'll test with our dedicated 2xA100 node profiles and also run a hosted fallback. benchmarks will include token throughput (tokens/sec), request p50/p95/p99 latencies, and error rate under sustained bursts.
[03:30] Amira Patel: timeline? we want to finish pilot validation within 2 weeks and then move to a month-long soak if everything looks ok.
[03:38] Maya Chen: proposed timeline: this week share runbook + bench scripts, next week kickoff + 3-day smoke run, then full 7-day stress, final 2-3 day regression tests. total ~2 weeks active testing.
[03:52] Grace Liu: security gating: before we start active tests, we need a signed A N D A and network-allow list, plus confirmation on egress circuits.
[04:03] Maya Chen: understood, we'll attach a standard pilot terms template; legal team can redline.
[04:08] Owen Park: how do you measure data residency? we need to ensure no tokens leave region and no calls route to non-authorized peered accounts.
[04:18] Luis Ortega: measurement approach: we run packet-level checks on both sides and validate internal trace IDs and region tags. Redwood Console will surface per-request region attribution. note - console name sometimes shows as "redwood console" or shorthand in our logs, but we'll point to the exact field.
[04:34] Jon Ruiz: bench detail: we want to replay 7 days of production traffic (anonymized) for a long soak, but for initial test we'll use synthetic with heavy tails (to simulate bursts). can you support replaying a gzipped event stream via s3 presigned URL?
[04:50] Luis Ortega: yes we support S3-based replay. for private network we'll ask you to either host the data in a shared s3 in same region or we can pull via a privatelink endpoint — we'll provide instructions.
[05:02] Amira Patel: any known gotchas with KV cache or HTTP2 multiplexing? we rely on KV cache for context reuse.
[05:09] Luis Ortega: KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K V cash) is supported; important detail: when you use large context lengths the cache hit pattern and memory pressure change. we'll instrument cache hit ratios and share recommendations (e.g., rolling window size). HTTP2 multiplex sometimes needs tuning on the client side — we'll include client settings in the runbook.
[05:30] Grace Liu: encryption in transit — TLS standards, mutual auth? we need mTLS to our endpoints.
[05:36] Maya Chen: we can enable mTLS on privatelink endpoints; for peering mutual TLS is generally at the app layer, but we can provide cert mgmt guidance.
[05:46] Owen Park: SLA targets — we need p99 400ms for 8k and 700ms for 16k during pilot; are those achievable?
[05:56] Luis Ortega: based on similar workloads, p99 400ms on 8k is feasible with dedicated capacity and tuned batching. 16k is harder, expect p99 in the 600-900ms range depending on token lengths and backend kernel selection. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching knobs to meet those SLOs.
[06:16] Jon Ruiz: benchmark sample metrics to capture: tokens/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utl, queue depth, and error types. also capture cost per 1M tokens for comparison.
[06:28] Luis Ortega: agreed. we'll push a sample spreadsheet that collects those fields.
[06:34] Amira Patel: how do we handle failover if the dedicated pool hits capacity? we want deterministic fallback policy.
[06:41] Maya Chen: Redwood can route to a lower-cost hosted variant or a smaller model variant for graceful degradation. For pilot we'll configure canary fallback with tracing enabled so you can see when fallback happened.
[06:55] Grace Liu: auditability — we need per-call user identity and retention for 90 days. can you confirm retention windows and S3 export to our audit account?
[07:05] Luis Ortega: yes logs can be exported to your S3 with configurable retention; default pilot retention can be 90 days, and we'll show how to snapshot and hand over.
[07:15] Jon Ruiz: network specifics we need to provide: VPC CIDRs, route table owners, security group maintainers, and who will approve prefix lists.
[07:25] Amira Patel: we'll share an architecture diagram — noting we use multiple AZs in the region and want the service to be pinned to us regionally.
[07:33] Luis Ortega: region pinning: we can pin to a single region and deny cross-region replication; in our telemetry we'll record region on each request. slight transcribe issue sometimes shows "region pinning" as "region pinningg" in auto notes.
[07:47] Maya Chen: ok let's lock success criteria. proposed: 1) p99 latency <= 400ms for 8k under your peak burst profile for 72% of runs, 2) sustained throughput matching 600 qps for 1 minute windows without errors over 95% of the time, 3) no egress to non-authorized regions in packet-level checks, and 4) audit logs and BYOK functioning.
[08:15] Owen Park: sounds reasonable. can you quantify "72% of runs"?
[08:20] Luis Ortega: it's a pragmatic cutoff to show stability under burst variability; we can instead set a target of 90th percentile of runs meeting p99 < 400ms — happy to align on whichever you prefer.
[08:33] Amira Patel: let's go with 90th percentile of test windows meeting the p99 target.
[08:39] Maya Chen: noted. next: bench schedule and responsibilities — we'll send the harness, you'll schedule a maintenance window for the smoke test, then we'll run the 7-day stress as discussed.
[08:50] Jon Ruiz: during smoke, we'll also run a simulated failover test to ensure canary fallback works and logs capture the event.
[08:57] Luis Ortega: good — include a step where we intentionally throttle a node to observe degradation and fallback. we'll provide the fault-injection commands.
[09:08] Grace Liu: when you say "fault injection" are we using off-the-shelf tools or your scripts? we need to audit commands for compliance.
[09:16] Luis Ortega: we'll provide sanitized scripts and a runbook entry for the test, and they can run from your side to keep full audit chain.
[09:26] Maya Chen: any blockers on the list?
[09:29] Amira Patel: we need detailed cost estimate for privatelink vs peering at our traffic levels before legal signs off.
[09:36] Luis Ortega: action: we'll create a cost model spreadsheet for both topologies showing data processing and per-hour endpoint costs.
[09:43] Owen Park: availability window? we need 99.9% during business hours. can you map that to infra?
[09:50] Luis Ortega: Dedicated pools with cross-AZ redundancy typically hit 99.9% for serving; we'll show historical uptime numbers in the proposal.
[09:59] Jon Ruiz: do you have any existing customers with similar regulatory profiles? would like a reference.
[10:04] Maya Chen: yes we have healthcare customers in NA and EU; we'll share two anonymized references and an SOC2 copy under NDA.
[10:12] Grace Liu: ok, send me the SOC2 contact and the retention policy doc.
[10:16] Maya Chen: will do.
[10:19] Amira Patel: final ask — can we schedule the pilot kickoff next tuesday at 09:00 PT?
[10:25] Maya Chen: i'll check Redwood's calendar and propose the slot, sounds doable.
[10:30] Luis Ortega: recap of technical deliverables: runbook + bench scripts, privatelink vs peering cost model, sample benchmark spreadsheet, fault injection scripts, S3 replay instructions, and region pinning verification steps.
[10:45] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and next steps.
[10:52] Amira Patel: thanks all.
[10:55] transcript_end: true
